title: Third-Person Singular Present Agreement
description: In the present tense, third-person singular subjects (he, she, it, singular nouns) require verbs ending in -s or -es (e.g., 'does', 'writes', 'goes'). The negative auxiliary is 'does not' or 'doesn't', never 'don't'.
pedagogical_tip: Check if the subject is singular (he/she/it). If yes, pair it with 'does' / 'doesn't'.

title: Past Simple with Explicit Time Markers
description: When an action was completed in the past and is accompanied by a past time indicator (e.g., 'yesterday', 'last week', 'in 2020'), use the simple past tense form of the verb rather than the base or present form.

examples.incorrect: She go to the store yesterday.
examples.correct: She went to the store yesterday.

pedagogical_tip: Watch for past time adverbs like 'yesterday' or 'ago' and conjugate the main verb to simple past.

title: Indefinite Article Selection (A vs. An)
description: Use 'a' before words starting with a consonant sound, and 'an' before words starting with a vowel sound.
pedagogical_tip: Base article choice on the spoken initial sound, not just the written letter.

title: Quantifier and Plural Noun Concord
description: Cardinal numbers greater than one (two, three, etc.) and plural determiners (several, many) require plural countable nouns.
pedagogical_tip: Verify that countable nouns following numbers > 1 carry their plural inflection (-s or -es).

title: Directional and Positional Prepositions
description: Verbs of motion such as 'go', 'travel', or 'walk' take 'to' when indicating destination, whereas stationary actions take 'at' or 'in'.
pedagogical_tip: Use 'to' with movements toward a target; use 'at' or 'in' for fixed locations.
